title: Exposure Handbrake Mini-Canvas and Evacuation Flow
creator: Aisha Rahman
description: Design a compact, low-friction control surface (mini-canvas) for quick staged rollouts and an "evacuation" or emergency rewind flow. The mini-canvas sits in the Console header for routes and allows engineers to start lightweight experiments (canary/A-B/traffic-splits) with sensible defaults, visible safety gates, and a one-click emergency handbrake that immediately re-routes traffic back to the stable variant and surfaces a rollback incident card.
acceptance_criteria: Mini-canvas prototype (desktop) with create/edit quick path for canary, A/B, and split experiments
Emergency rewind modal that cancels active experiments and documents reason and rollback scope
Percent slider with single-token keyboard control and live cost delta estimation
Signal thresholds UI (latency/error/accuracy) + inline suggestions for safe stop levels
Telemetry hooks defined for events: experiment_start, traffic_adjust, emergency_rewind, experiment_end
Accessibility: keyboard-first interactions, ARIA labels for critical controls
engineering_notes: Prototype assumes existing rollout API endpoints: /v1/rollouts:start, /v1/rollouts:update, /v1/rollouts:stop
Cost delta uses token-rate estimates from billing service; show conservative and optimistic ranges
Emergency rewind triggers a high-priority rollback job; needs idempotent behavior and audit log entry
Recommend adding a rate-limited ‘panic’ audit event to trace operator actions across orgs
decisions: Place mini-canvas in route header rather than left nav to minimize context switch
Default experiment length set to 24 hours with an opt-in extended option
Emergency rewind will default to 'stable' variant and capture incident metadata before action
Show cost delta only on open canvas to reduce noise in route listing pages
